analysis.investment_thesis: Piccadily is a genuinely good business with a rising ROIC (~22.7%) and exceptional margin expansion, anchored by the fast-growing Indri single malt brand — but at a ~3% earnings yield (EBIT/EV), the Magic Formula says you are massively overpaying. The deep-negative FCF of -270 Cr in FY2025 and a capex supercycle consuming earnings make the current price unjustifiable on any systematic value framework.
key_strengths: ROIC ~22.7% (EBIT/CE) and operating margin expanding to 25.9% — a legitimately high-quality business
Operating income CAGR of 25.9% over 9 years signals durable pricing power and premiumization (Indri, Camikara brands)
Promoter holding at 68.57% and reserves jumping from 245→706 Cr (FY24→25) suggest a successful equity raise funding real expansion
key_risks: Earnings yield (EBIT/EV) of ~3% — far below the 6% floor; the stock is priced for perfection with zero margin of safety
FCF was -270 Cr in FY2025 with capex of 243 Cr and OCF turning negative (-27 Cr) despite 102 Cr reported net profit — cash generation is currently an illusion
Net profit declined YoY (110→102 Cr) even as revenues grew 7.4%, and debt nearly doubled (172→324 Cr); the capex cycle must succeed or returns will compress sharply
red_flags: Earnings yield ~3% (EBIT 183 Cr / EV ~6,061 Cr) — deeply overvalued by Magic Formula
Negative operating cash flow (-27 Cr) and FCF (-270 Cr) in FY2025 despite ~102 Cr net profit signals aggressive working capital build or accounting distortion
CWIP surged from 42→242 Cr (FY24→25) — massive unproven capacity bet; if Indri demand disappoints, capital is stranded
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on Piccadily: EBIT (Operating Income) FY2025 = INR 183 Cr; Enterprise Value = Market Cap (5,762 Cr) + Net Debt (299 Cr) ≈ 6,061 Cr. Earnings Yield = 183/6,061 = **3.0%** — less than one-quarter of my 12% attractiveness threshold. Return on Capital using stated ROCE = **22.7%** — decent, clearing the 20% bar, but not exceptional. A good business at a terrible price is still a bad investment. The Magic Formula's entire insight is that you need BOTH cheapness AND quality; Piccadily delivers only one half of that equation.

The operational picture has a serious cash flow disconnect: FY2025 net profit was 102 Cr, yet OCF was -27 Cr and FCF was -270 Cr. This is explained by 243 Cr of capex (CWIP: 42→242 Cr) and likely heavy working capital absorption in the distillery/aging business. The company raised ~460 Cr in equity (reserves 245→706 Cr) to fund this expansion — a calculated bet on Indri's premiumization story. That bet may well pay off in 3-5 years, but today's valuation (P/E 43x, P/S 6x) already prices in near-perfection. Greenblatt's formula demands I wait until the market offers this business at a price where earnings yield reaches at least 10-12%; at INR 585, we are nowhere close.
